primary_findings: The split raw/canonical body shape was stable across all eight specimens.
All eight specimens kept canonical_semantic_pointer null unless operator, object class, and object version were all registry-backed.
One gpt-5.4-mini specimen blocked CREATE along with the unregistered object/version, showing that independent component admission needs to be explicit.
Version candidate shape remains ambiguous: some outputs used token-only versions while others used object-bound version refs.
recommended_next_iteration: Add an explicit independent-component D-law: blocking one component must not erase other admitted components.
Split raw_object_version_candidate into raw_object_version_token_candidate and raw_object_version_ref_candidate.
Keep canonical_object_version_ref as the admitted registry-backed value.
Add bait that suggests nulling the admitted operator when object/version admission fails.
overall_assessment: Probe 016 supports the raw/canonical split and full-pointer fail-closed rule, but it exposes two schema hardening needs: independent component admission and clearer version-token/ref fields.
